chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), regarding the saying:
of Allah, the Exalted: “A questioner asked for a punishment bound to befall. For the disbelievers in the wilayah of Ali, there is none to avert it.”
Then he said: “Thus, by Allah, Jibra'il (عليه السلام) descended with it upon Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله).”

key_terms.الْكَافِرِينَ: those who disbelieve or reject the truth being referenced here
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibra'il, the angel who brings revelation
key_terms.دَافِعٌ: one who can repel or avert something
key_terms.عَذَابٍ وَاقِعٍ: an inevitable punishment that will surely occur
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٍ: the Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله)
key_terms.وَلَايَةِ عَلِيٍّ: the divinely appointed authority and guardianship of Ali (عليه السلام)

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith interpret "سَأَلَ سَائِلٌ بِعَذَابٍ وَاقِعٍ" in relation to the wilayah of Ali (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a tafsir reading of the opening verses as referring specifically to rejection of the wilayah of Ali (عليه السلام). It emphasizes, in Shia tradition, the theological centrality of wilayah and attributes this wording to revelation brought by Jibra'il (عليه السلام) to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Suleyman, from his father, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted
[70:1] A questioner, asked for the Punishment to befall [70:2] For the unbelievers in the Wilayah of Aliasws, there is none to avert it’.
Then heasws said: ‘This is how, by Allahazwj Jibraeelas descended with it unto Muhammadsaww’.
en.sarwar: 47. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Sayf from his brother from his father from abu Hamza from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most High.
“. . your ideas are confused [51:8]. Let whoever wishes, turn away from it (Wilaya, Leadership with Divine Authority) (Our Quran).” [51:9]
The Imam (a.s.) said, “whoever would turn away from Wilaya, (Leadership with Divine Authority) he has turned away from paradise.”
